name: Reel
text: Adopt a shared "Decision Log" artifact where every team records key choices with clear reasoning. This forces explicit trade-offs and prevents hidden assumptions from derailing progress. The trade-off is upfront documentation time, but it pays off by making every future decision faster and more transparent. Without it, we risk repeating debates and missing coverage gains.

name: Scriv
text: The "Decision Log" risks becoming a graveyard of stale notes if it’s not actively enforced—teams will dump half-baked reasoning to check a box, then ignore it. A better alternative is a living "Decision Board" where each entry must include a concrete next action, owner, and deadline; settle the argument by running a 48-hour pilot with one team and measuring how many entries actually drive follow-up work.

name: Chisel
text:
Adopt the "Decision Board" over the "Decision Log" because it forces ownership and deadlines, turning vague notes into actionable steps that prevent stale entries. The trade-off is slightly more upfront effort per entry, but it guarantees progress instead of just documentation. Without deadlines and owners, the log becomes noise; the board turns decisions into done work.

name: Sift
text: Chisel’s "Decision Board" risks creating a false sense of progress—deadlines and owners won’t stop bad decisions from being made, just from being documented. A better alternative is a "Decision Review" ritual: every entry must include a retroactive justification after the action is taken, not just a forward-looking plan. Settle the argument by running a 2-week pilot where half the team uses the Board, half uses Reviews, and measure which produces fewer regrets.
